turns.content: Two unknown starting materials share the skeleton HOOC-CH2-CH(Et)-CH2-COOiBu. Reaction A uses LiBH4 followed by H+ to give (R)-4-ethyltetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-one, whereas reaction B uses BH3 followed by H+ to give the (S) lactone. Identify the reducible terminal groups and note what happens, or does not happen, at C3 in each sequence.

For the starting monoacid monoester, the relevant C3 priority order is ester-side chain > acid-side chain > ethyl > hydrogen. Explain the CIP comparison between the two carbonyl-containing chains and how this ordering is used to assign an R or S descriptor.
Trace reaction A. Which terminal group does LiBH4 reduce, which original side provides the lactone carbonyl after workup, and what is the product-side CIP order at the unchanged C3 geometry?
Now trace reaction B. Which terminal group does BH3 reduce, which original side provides the lactone carbonyl after workup, and what is the product-side CIP order at the unchanged C3 geometry?
Compare the two product-side priority orders with the stated R and S lactones, then determine the required starting configurations of A and B without invoking any bond change at C3.
Verify both assignments by tracing LiBH4 ester reduction, BH3 carboxylic-acid reduction, lactonization, and the resulting CIP priorities.
Give the full identities and configurations of starting materials A and B.
